name: 挖仓坡
Dig Slope
before: 一面荒坡被挖得像筛子，几十个假和尚抡着锄头，坑挨着坑。他们在找「千里仓」：传说千里号当年留下的粮，不止碑上写的三百石，还有一座藏粮的仓，谁找到谁就是粥棚的主。挖了一个月，挖出来的只有碎陶片和一窝跳鼠。监工的打手见你们来了，把锄头一横。

A barren slope has been dug into a sieve: dozens of false monks swinging hoes, pit beside pit. They're hunting for the Qianli Granary. Legend says the caravan left more than the three hundred measures on the stele; there was a whole granary, and whoever finds it owns the porridge shed. A month of digging has turned up potsherds and a nest of jerboas. Their overseers see you coming and level their hoes.
after: 打手们被打散，假和尚扔了锄头就跑。坡下一个歇脚的老香客笑出了眼泪：「傻子，粮仓哪有挖在土里的？戈壁上的土一返潮，粮全霉了。千佛洞的东西，要么在崖上，要么在窟里。」他指了指东边的山：「守粥师父也这么说过。」

The overseers scattered, the false monks drop their hoes and run. An old pilgrim resting below laughs till he cries. 'Fools. Who digs a granary into the ground? One damp spell on this plain and the grain all rots. Everything at the caves is either up on the cliff or inside a cave.' He points at the hills to the east. 'Master Shouzhou said the same.'

name: 三百碗架
Rack of Three Hundred Bowls
before: 粥棚后面一排木架，架上挂着三百只木碗，每只碗底刻着一个名字。几个假和尚正把碗一只只摘下来装进筐，说是「千里号圣碗」，拿到关内能卖大价钱。架子底下，那个半聋的老火头拦着筐不放，被推了一个跟头，爬起来又拦。

Behind the porridge shed stands a long wooden rack hung with three hundred wooden bowls, a name carved into the bottom of each. False monks are unhooking them into baskets: 'sacred bowls of the Qianli caravan', worth a fortune back inside the Pass. The half-deaf old cook keeps blocking the basket. They knock him over; he gets up and blocks it again.
after: 假和尚被打跑，老火头把碗一只只挂回去。他说，那年冬天三百人天天在这儿喝粥，白天上崖修栈道、抹墙泥，「喝我一碗粥，还我一天工」。碗他每晚都洗，洗了十年。架子尽头还有一只没刻名字的碗，是当年烧火的小和尚的，「他喝得最多，后来不来了」。

The false monks chased off, the old cook hangs the bowls back one by one. That winter, he shouts, the three hundred ate porridge here every day and went up the cliff by day to build walkways and plaster walls. 'A bowl of my porridge, a day of their work.' He has washed every bowl every night for ten years. At the very end hangs one bowl with no name: it belonged to the little monk who tended the fire back then. 'He ate the most. Then he stopped coming.'

name: 守粥庵
Shouzhou's Hut
before: 山脚死胡同里一间小庵，是守粥师父住的地方，门口种着一畦豆子。一伙假和尚正在庵里翻箱倒柜，连灶膛都掏空了，要找钱满仓说的「续粮的线索」。门框上挂着一串干豆子编的念珠，被他们扯断了，豆子滚了一地。

Down a dead end at the foot of the hill is a small hermitage, Master Shouzhou's, with a patch of beans planted by the door. False monks are ransacking it, even raking out the stove, hunting for the 'grain clue' Qian Mancang told them about. A rosary of dried beans hung on the door frame; they've torn it and the beans have rolled everywhere.
after: 假和尚被撵走，你们在灶台上找到一张纸条，是守粥的字：「上山找续粮的人，三日回。豆子看家。」日子是两个月前的。纸条底下还有一行歪歪扭扭的小字，显然是孩子写的：「豆子不看家。豆子去找师父。」

With the false monks thrown out, you find a note on the stove in Shouzhou's hand: 'Gone up the mountain to find whoever sends the grain. Back in three days. Douzi, mind the house.' It's dated two months ago. Below it, in a wobbly child's hand: 'Douzi is not minding the house. Douzi has gone to find Master.'

name: 叫花坛
The Beggars' Court
before: 一座破土地庙前围了上百个乞丐，正在开「叫花大会」，审的是金身寺的假和尚：粥要了钱，叫花子喝不起，这是断了他们的活路。几个被抓来的假和尚跪在当中，可金身寺的打手也赶到了，两边抄起了打狗棍和短刀，眼看就要打成一锅粥。

Hundreds of beggars crowd before a ruined shrine for a Beggars' Assembly, and on trial are the false monks of the Golden Body Temple: charging for porridge beggars can't afford is taking away their living. A few captured false monks kneel in the middle. But the temple's toughs have arrived, and both sides have their dog-sticks and knives out. It's about to turn into a brawl.
after: 打手被打退，叫花子们拍手叫好，把假和尚轰回了金身寺。丐头是个独眼老汉，他说他每年秋天都睡在粥棚后头，见过那辆夜里来的粮车：赶牛的人戴着铜面具，不打火把，卸了粮就往东北的戈壁里走，「脚底下一点声儿没有，跟巡夜的兵一样」。

The toughs beaten back, the beggars cheer and run the false monks home. Their chief, a one-eyed old man, sleeps behind the porridge shed every autumn and has seen the night cart. The men driving the oxen wear bronze masks and carry no torches; once the grain is down they head off north-east into the gravel desert. 'Not a sound from their feet. Like soldiers on night watch.'

name: 窟前市
The Market Below the Caves
before: 崖下一片空场，从前是千佛洞最热闹的集：凿窟的石匠们挑着凿下来的石料出来卖，香客和山下的庄户拿粮食来换，换了石头回去垒墙、砌灶、修猪圈。如今钱满仓的打手在场口设了卡，粮食进场要抽三成，石匠们饿得凿不动，石料堆成了山也卖不出去。

Below the cliff lies an open square that was once the liveliest market at the caves. The cave carvers would carry out the stone they'd cut and sell it, and pilgrims and farmers from below would bring grain to trade for it, taking the stone home for walls, stoves and pigsties. Now Qian Mancang's toughs have set up a checkpoint at the entrance and take three tenths of all grain coming in. The carvers are too hungry to cut, and the stone piles up unsold.
after: 打手们被赶走，窟前市重新开了张：粮食一担担挑进来，换走崖下的石料，每天的交易又热闹起来。一个老石匠捧着一碗粥蹲在石堆上说，那年冬天千里号的人跟他们一起凿石、一起扛，三百人顶得上三百个匠人，「他们走的时候，说石头是佛的，粮食是人的，换一换，两边都饿不着」。他还说钱满仓带着半张图往东山跑了，「找千里仓去了」。

With the toughs driven off, the market opens again: grain comes in by the shoulder-load and leaves as stone, and the daily trade is lively once more. An old stonemason squats on a stone pile with a bowl of porridge. That winter, he says, the Qianli caravan cut and carried stone alongside them, three hundred men as good as three hundred masons. 'When they left they said the stone belongs to the Buddha and the grain belongs to people. Trade one for the other and neither goes hungry.' And Qian Mancang has run off into the eastern hills with half a map, he adds. 'Gone looking for the Qianli Granary.'

name: 水磨坊
The Water Mill
before: 渠边一座水磨坊，磨盘日夜转，磨的是粥棚的粮。金身寺的人押着磨坊老板，逼他每磨一斗米掺半斗锯末，「粥稠不稠，香客看不出来」。老板不肯，磨坊的门就被钉死了，他和他的驴一起被关在里面。门外守着一伙打手，吃着老板家的炒豆子。

A water mill by the irrigation channel grinds the porridge shed's grain day and night. The Golden Body Temple's men are forcing the miller to cut every measure of grain with half a measure of sawdust: 'Pilgrims can't tell how thick it is.' He refused, so they nailed his door shut with him and his donkey inside. Toughs sit outside eating his roasted beans.
after: 打手被打跑，你们撬开门，老板和驴一起冲了出来。他说那些盖着金面印的粮袋，粮食跟山下的不一样：粒小、壳硬，夹着沙子，是戈壁边上开荒种出来的，「种的人不会种地，可一年比一年种得好」。他递过一袋新磨的面：「十年来最干净的一袋。」

The toughs chased off, you prise open the door and the miller and his donkey burst out together. The grain in those mask-stamped sacks isn't like the grain from down here, he says: small, hard-hulled, gritty with sand, grown on land broken at the edge of the desert. 'Whoever grows it doesn't know farming. But it gets better every year.' He hands you a bag of fresh flour. 'Cleanest bag I've ground in ten years.'

name: 锁僧窟
The Locked Cave
before: 山脚的一个小窟口被木栅钉死了，里面传出念经声，念得有气无力。钱满仓把不肯入伙的真和尚都关在这里，每天只送一碗清水。窟口守着几个假和尚，嗑着瓜子，隔一会儿往里喊一声：「想通了没有？剃了头的，跟谁不是吃饭？」

A small cave mouth at the foot of the hill has been boarded up, and from inside comes chanting, weak and tired. Qian Mancang has locked up all the real monks who wouldn't join him here, with one bowl of water a day. A few false monks guard the entrance cracking melon seeds, calling in every so often: 'Changed your minds yet? You've shaved your heads, what's it matter whose rice you eat?'
after: 假和尚被赶跑，你们拆了木栅，十几个真和尚扶着墙走出来，头一句问的是：「粥棚开着吗？」他们说钱满仓最怕山上的金面，金面不出山，他才敢占粥棚。守粥师父被关前说过，正路有金面卫拦着，他要从东边山沟绕上去，「当面问问，粮还送不送」。

With the false monks gone you tear down the boards, and a dozen real monks feel their way out along the wall. Their first question: 'Is the porridge shed open?' What Qian Mancang fears most is the Gold Mask on the mountain, they say; only because the Gold Mask never comes down has he dared to take the shed. Before they were locked up, Master Shouzhou said the Gold Masks were blocking the main path, so he'd go round by the eastern gullies 'and ask to his face whether the grain will keep coming'.

name: 伐杨林
The Felled Poplars
before: 一溜胡杨林里响着斧子声，金身寺的人在砍树，砍下来的胡杨劈成柴，拉回去熬他们一钱一碗的稀粥。胡杨的木头硬，砍一棵要半天，他们就先砍边上的，林子边已经秃了一片，沙子顺着缺口往里灌。一个看林子的老汉抱着树不肯撒手，被打得鼻青脸肿。

Axes ring through a line of desert poplars. The Golden Body Temple's men are felling them for firewood to boil their coin-a-bowl gruel. Poplar wood is hard, half a day a tree, so they take the edge trees first; the margin of the wood is already bald and sand is pouring in through the gap. An old forester hugs a trunk and won't let go, and has been beaten black and blue for it.
after: 砍树的被赶跑，老汉摸着树皮说：胡杨不靠天上的雨活，根往下扎，一直扎到地下水里，所以胡杨长成一溜的地方，底下准有一条看不见的水，多半是从前的河道。砍了它，沙就进来了。他指给你们看一棵树上新刻的字：「守粥过此」，旁边一个箭头，指着东边。

With the woodcutters chased off, the old man strokes the bark. Poplars don't live on rain, he says; their roots go down and down until they reach the groundwater, so wherever poplars grow in a line there's an unseen stream beneath, most likely an old river course. Cut them and the sand moves in. He shows you fresh letters carved into one trunk, 'Shouzhou passed here', and an arrow pointing east.

name: 钱家仓
The Qian Granary
before: 死胡同尽头一座大仓，是钱满仓真正的家底：仓里堆的是这一年从粥棚扣下来的粮，还有截下的夜粮车，堆得顶到了房梁。他雇了一伙关内的刀客看仓，步、弩、骑都有，个个吃得红光满面。仓门口挂着一块新牌子：「荒年平价，概不赊欠」。

At the end of a dead end stands a big granary, Qian Mancang's real fortune: a year's grain skimmed from the porridge shed and the night carts he seized, piled to the rafters. He's hired swordsmen from inside the Pass to guard it, foot, crossbow and horse, all ruddy and well fed. A new sign hangs at the door: 'Fair prices in lean years. No credit.'
after: 刀客们被打散，仓里的粮一车车拉回了粥棚。你们翻出钱满仓的账本，上面算得清清楚楚：等哪年遭了灾，粮价翻五倍再卖。账本最后一页贴着半张图，图上画着东山的一道崖，崖上一个圈，旁边写：「千里仓，得其半，余半在守粥处。」

The swordsmen scattered, the grain goes back to the porridge shed cart by cart. Qian Mancang's ledger lays out his plan precisely: wait for a disaster year and sell at five times the price. On its last page is pasted half a map: a cliff in the eastern hills with a circle on it and the note 'Qianli Granary. Half obtained. The other half is with Shouzhou.'

name: 拦山卡
The Mountain Barrier
before: 上山的正路被一队金面卫截住了，刀卫守在石阶上，弩手伏在崖缝里。他们不收钱，也不说为什么，只说一句：「洞主有令，山下的人不许上山。」一个香客想塞给他们一串钱，被原样塞了回来。

The main path up the mountain is cut by a troop of Gold Masks: swordsmen on the stone steps, crossbowmen hidden in cracks in the cliff. They don't take money and won't say why, only: 'The Lord's orders. No one from below goes up.' A pilgrim tries to slip them a string of coins and has it pushed straight back into his hand.
after: 金面卫退上了山，领头的一个倒是多说了几句：两个月前有个胖和尚扛着一只空粮袋来，说要见洞主，他们没放，「洞主说过，谁都不放」。胖和尚就往东去了，说绕东沟上山。领头的沉默了一会儿，又说：「东沟有豹子。你们要是往那边走，替我们看一眼。」

The Gold Masks withdraw up the mountain, though their leader says a little more. Two months ago a fat monk came with an empty grain sack asking to see the Lord. They didn't let him through: 'The Lord said no one.' So the fat monk went east, saying he'd go up by the eastern gully. The leader is quiet a moment, then adds: 'There are leopards in the eastern gully. If you're going that way, have a look for us.'

name: 豆腐坊
The Tofu Shop
before: 路边一家豆腐坊，石磨、大锅、一排压豆腐的木框。一伙开了小差的兵痞占了作坊，天天逼着豆腐娘子点豆腐，点出来就吃，吃完了再点，一个月吃掉了全村一冬的黄豆。豆腐娘子说再吃下去，就只能拿豆渣喂他们了。

A tofu shop by the road: stone quern, big cauldron, a row of wooden pressing frames. A band of deserters has moved in and makes the tofu woman curdle batch after batch, eating it as fast as she makes it. In a month they've eaten the whole village's winter soybeans. Any more and she'll be feeding them the dregs.
after: 兵痞被撵走，豆腐娘子长出一口气，石磨又转了起来。她说豆子那孩子，是九年前守粥师父在粥棚的豆子袋里捡到的，所以叫豆子。前几天豆子路过这里，背着一袋黄豆往东走，「说是一路撒豆子，师父回头就能找着他，他回头也能找着师父」。

The deserters run out, the tofu woman breathes again and the quern turns. Douzi, she tells you, was found nine years ago by Master Shouzhou in a sack of beans at the porridge shed; hence the name, which means Little Bean. A few days ago Douzi came by heading east with a bag of soybeans on his back. 'He said he'd drop beans all the way, so Master could find him if he turned back, and he could find Master.'
first: 兵痞们的铺盖底下抄出十二斤腊肉、三坛酸菜、一口偷来的铁锅、七件抢来的皮袄，还有一包豆腐娘子的卤水，他们怕她跑了，连点豆腐的卤都锁了起来。

Under the deserters' bedding you find twelve pounds of cured meat, three crocks of pickled cabbage, a stolen iron wok, seven looted sheepskin coats, and the tofu woman's bag of brine. They'd locked even her curdling salts away so she couldn't run.
pass: 每次路过，豆腐娘子都端出一锅热豆花，浇一勺辣子，再给你们包几张晾干的豆腐皮：「路上泡水就能吃，比干粮软和。」

Every time you pass, the tofu woman brings out a pot of hot bean curd with a spoonful of chilli on top and wraps up sheets of dried tofu skin for you. 'Soak them on the road and they're ready. Softer than hard rations.'

name: 拾豆营
Bean-Pickers' Camp
before: 一伙逃兵扎营在路边，营里一个人捧着一碗黄豆，一颗颗地数。他们是钱满仓雇来找守粥师父的，手里有一张和尚的画像，画得像个冬瓜。他们发现了路上撒的豆子，一路捡过来，越捡越近，见你们也盯着地上的豆子，以为是来抢功的。

Deserters are camped by the road, and one of them sits counting soybeans out of a bowl. Qian Mancang hired them to find Master Shouzhou; they have a portrait of the monk that looks like a winter melon. They spotted the beans scattered along the road and have been picking them up as they follow, getting closer all the time. Seeing you also looking at the beans on the ground, they think you're after their reward.
after: 逃兵被打散，数豆子的那个交代：豆子一路撒到了东边的沟口，他们在沟口逮住了一个小沙弥，交给了钱满仓的人，「说是拿小的当饵，大的自己会出来」。他把那碗豆子还给你们：「捡了三百多颗，一颗没吃。」

The deserters scattered, the bean counter confesses. The trail ran to the mouth of a gully in the east, where they caught a little novice and handed him to Qian Mancang's men. 'Use the little one as bait and the big one will come out by himself.' He gives you the bowl of beans. 'Picked up three hundred and some. Didn't eat a single one.'

name: 喝粥坡
Porridge-Raised Slope
before: 坡上拦路的是一伙半大小子，骑着偷来的骆驼，刀是捡来的，脸还没长开。他们都是在千里粥棚喝粥长大的孤儿，粥要了钱，他们喝不起，就学人劫道。领头的十六七岁，喊「留下买路钱」的时候嗓子还在变声，喊劈了。

The road over the slope is blocked by a pack of half-grown lads on stolen camels, with knives they found and faces not yet finished growing. They're orphans raised on the Qianli porridge. Now that it costs money they can't afford it, so they've taken up robbery. Their leader is sixteen or seventeen, and when he shouts 'Pay the toll!' his breaking voice cracks.
after: 小子们被打下骆驼，倒也服气，听说粥棚又不要钱了，眼睛都亮了。领头的说守粥师父教他们认字，就是照着那三百只木碗底下的名字认的，「我认的头一个字是『曹』」。他们发誓回去替粥棚看门，又说上个月看见守粥师父背着空袋子往东沟去了。

Knocked off their camels, the lads take it well, and when they hear the porridge is free again their eyes light up. Master Shouzhou taught them to read, the leader says, from the names on the bottoms of those three hundred bowls. 'The first character I learned was Cao.' They swear to go back and guard the shed's door, and say that last month they saw Master Shouzhou heading for the eastern gully with an empty sack on his back.

name: 羊肠道
Goat Track
before: 东沟口的山道窄得只容一只羊过，钱满仓剩下的打手守在这里，等着守粥师父从山上下来。他们在路上拉了绊马索，崖上堆了石头，自己蹲在背风处啃干饼。路边的石缝里，卡着几颗黄豆。

At the mouth of the eastern gully the track narrows to the width of a goat. Qian Mancang's remaining toughs wait here for Master Shouzhou to come down: tripropes stretched across the path, rocks piled on the cliff above, the men crouched out of the wind gnawing dry flatbread. In the cracks of the rocks by the path, a few soybeans are wedged.
after: 打手们被赶下了山道。你们顺着石缝里的豆子往上找，在一块大石头背面捡到一串念珠，是干豆子编的，和守粥庵门框上那串一模一样，只是绳子断了一半。豆子一路往沟里去，越撒越稀，像是撒的人舍不得了。

The toughs are driven off the track. Following the beans in the cracks upward, you find behind a boulder a rosary of dried beans, the twin of the one on the hermitage door frame, its string half broken. The beans lead on into the gully, more and more sparsely, as if whoever was dropping them had started to run short.

name: 饵僧桩
The Bait Post
before: 沟口一棵枯胡杨上绑着个八九岁的小沙弥，面前摆着一只空碗，碗里插了一根筷子，是钱满仓的人摆的「招魂碗」，说守粥师父心疼徒弟，看见了准下山。小沙弥倒不哭，正冲着看守的打手背《心经》，背一句，打手就捂一回耳朵。

Tied to a dead poplar at the mouth of the gully is a little novice of eight or nine, an empty bowl in front of him with a chopstick stuck upright in it: Qian Mancang's men call it the 'summoning bowl'. Master Shouzhou loves his pupil, so when he sees it he'll surely come down. The novice isn't crying. He's reciting the Heart Sutra at his guards, and at every line a guard covers his ears.
after: 看守被打跑，你们解开绳子，小沙弥揉着手腕自报家门：「我叫豆子，我找师父。」他从怀里掏出一个瘪了的豆袋，里面只剩七颗豆子。他说师父临走前讲过，「粮是从东边来的，人也要往东边找」，他不肯回去：「你们不带我，我自己走。」

The guards chased off, you untie the rope and the novice rubs his wrists and introduces himself. 'I'm Douzi. I'm looking for my master.' From his robe he pulls a flat bean bag with seven beans left in it. Before he left, Master said, 'The grain comes from the east, so you look for people in the east too.' He won't go back. 'If you won't take me, I'll go by myself.'

name: 钱满仓
Qian Mancang
before: 一块大石头上蹲着一个胖和尚，脸上的金漆还没掉干净：正是金身寺的方丈钱满仓。他雇的人跑得只剩几个，干粮早吃光了，饿得两眼发直，怀里却还死死抱着半张图。剩下的几个打手正商量着，把他和图一起卖给盗经贼。

A fat monk crouches on a big rock, gold paint still not quite off his face: Qian Mancang, abbot of the Golden Body Temple. His hirelings have mostly run off, his food is long gone and he's dizzy with hunger, but he still clutches half a map to his chest. The few toughs he has left are discussing selling him and the map together to the sutra thieves.
after: 打手们被打跑，钱满仓瘫在石头上。豆子从袋里摸出两颗豆子，塞进他嘴里。钱满仓哭了：三年前他的粮栈倒了，在千里粥棚喝了一个月的粥才活过来，「我就想，这么好的粥棚，要是姓钱该多好」。他把半张图交了出来：「另外半张在守粥那儿。」

With the toughs chased off, Qian Mancang slumps on the rock. Douzi fishes two beans out of his bag and pops them into the man's mouth. Qian Mancang bursts into tears. Three years ago his grain business collapsed and he survived on a month of the Qianli porridge. 'And I thought, a porridge shed this good, if only it were called Qian's.' He hands over his half of the map. 'The other half's with Shouzhou.'

name: 断阶崖
Broken Steps Cliff
before: 豆子数着剩下的豆子领路，一直走到一道崖下。崖上凿着一溜石阶，走到半截断了，断口下面的乱石里卡着一只草鞋，鞋底磨得只剩薄薄一层。豆子一眼认出那是师父的鞋。可乱石堆边上围着一群豺狗，正为一袋撒了的粮食龇牙咧嘴。

Counting his last beans, Douzi leads you to the foot of a cliff. A flight of steps is cut into it, broken off halfway up, and in the rubble below the break is wedged a straw sandal worn to a thin sole. Douzi knows it at once: his master's. But a pack of dholes circles the rubble, snarling over a sack of spilled grain.
after: 豺狗被赶散了。撒了的粮食是戈壁边上那种粒小壳硬的粮，袋子上盖着金面的红印。断口上方的崖壁上有人用石头划了一行字：「阶断，下不去。粮够吃。勿念。」豆子把最后七颗豆子都撒在了崖下：「师父，我来了。」

The dholes are scattered. The spilled grain is that small, hard-hulled desert-edge kind, the sack stamped with the Gold Mask's red seal. Above the break, someone has scratched a line into the rock with a stone: 'Steps broken, can't get down. Enough grain to eat. Don't worry.' Douzi scatters his last seven beans at the foot of the cliff. 'Master, I'm here.'

name: 千里仓
The Qianli Granary
before: 两半张图一拼，千里仓找到了：死胡同尽头的崖壁上，一排凿出来的仓洞，洞口用木板封着。可有人先到了一步：一伙关内的刀客从盗经贼那里买了消息，占了仓洞，步、弩、骑三路守着，等着撬开封板发一笔大财。

Put the two halves of the map together and there's the Qianli Granary: a row of storage chambers cut into the cliff at the end of a dead end, their mouths boarded up. But someone got here first. Swordsmen from inside the Pass bought the location from the sutra thieves and now hold the chambers, foot, crossbow and horse, waiting to prise off the boards and make their fortune.
after: 刀客们被打退，你们撬开封板：仓洞里只有空陶瓮。洞壁上刻着取粮的记号，头三年刻的是「千」字，刻到第三年秋天，瓮底朝天。从第四年起，记号换成了一张没有五官的面具，一年一个，刻了七个。千里号的粮三年就施完了，后七年的粥，是金面续上的。

The swordsmen beaten back, you prise off the boards. The chambers hold only rows of empty jars. On the walls are notches for every withdrawal of grain. For the first three years the mark is the character Qian, until in the third autumn the jars stand upside down. From the fourth year the mark becomes a mask with no features, one a year, seven in all. The Qianli caravan's grain lasted three years. The porridge of the seven years since was the Gold Mask's.

name: 豹子沟
Leopard Gully
before: 沟里的石头上全是爪印，崖缝里时不时闪过一双黄眼睛。每年冬天，山里的黄羊顺着这条沟下来找草，豹子就跟着黄羊下来，一窝一窝地守在沟里。附近的牧人丢了好几头羊，谁也不敢进沟。守粥师父要上山，就得从这里过。

Claw marks cover the stones of the gully, and a pair of yellow eyes flashes now and then in a crack in the cliff. Every winter the goitered gazelles come down this gully from the mountains looking for grass, and the leopards follow, family after family, lying in wait. The herders nearby have lost several sheep and no one dares go in. To get up the mountain, Master Shouzhou would have had to pass through here.
after: 这一回的豹子被赶回了山里，沟里安静了。豆子在一块石头底下捡到半块干粮，上面有一排牙印，是人的，不是豹子的：「师父咬东西就是这样，先咬边。」可豹子跟着黄羊走，黄羊每年冬天都下山，过一阵，这沟里还得再来清一回。

This time the leopards are driven back into the hills and the gully goes quiet. Under a rock Douzi finds half a dry cake with a row of tooth marks, human, not leopard. 'That's how Master eats. He always bites the edge first.' But the leopards follow the gazelles, and the gazelles come down every winter. Before long someone will have to clear this gully again.

name: 悬粥台
The Hanging Ledge
before: 断阶上面，崖腰有一道窄窄的石台，台上搭着个草棚，一缕炊烟往上飘。豆子仰着脖子喊了一声「师父」，草棚里探出一个瘦了一大圈的和尚。可崖下守着一伙盗经贼，他们看守粥师父在台上下不来，想等他饿死，好去翻他身边那只金面送的粮袋，说里面准有洞主的东西。

Above the broken steps is a narrow ledge halfway up the cliff with a straw shelter on it and a thread of cooking smoke rising. Douzi tilts back his head and calls 'Master!' and out of the shelter looks a monk grown much thinner. But a band of sutra thieves is waiting at the cliff foot. Seeing Master Shouzhou can't get down, they mean to wait until he starves and then go through the sack of grain the Gold Mask gave him; there must be something of the Lord's in it, they say.
after: 盗经贼被打散，你们接上断阶，把守粥师父扶了下来。豆子扑上去，师徒俩抱着哭了一场。守粥说他见到了洞主：洞主不肯下山，只说「粥照施，粮我送，人不出山」，又往他袋里装满了粮。下山时石阶断了，他就在台上熬粥，熬了一个多月。「他说千里号留的粮是给过路人的，粮吃完了，路不能断。」守粥望着东北：「他守着崖上那三百个人，守了十年，自己连碗粥都舍不得下山喝。你们见了他，告诉他山下的粥没断。」

The sutra thieves scattered, you mend the broken steps and help Master Shouzhou down. Douzi flings himself at him and master and pupil weep together. Shouzhou did see the Lord. He wouldn't come down, only said, 'The porridge goes on, I'll send the grain, nobody leaves the mountain,' and filled his sack. On the way down the steps gave way, and he has been cooking porridge on this ledge for over a month. 'He said the Qianli grain was meant for travellers, and when it ran out, the road mustn't be cut.' Shouzhou looks north-east. 'He's guarded those three hundred on the cliff for ten years and won't even come down for a bowl of porridge himself. When you see him, tell him the porridge below hasn't stopped.'

name: 拆梁坡
Beam Thieves' Slope
before: 一道矮崖上残留着半截旧栈道，木梁一根根插在崖壁的孔里。一伙关内木材商雇来的刀手正在拆，拆下来的梁码在车上，说是上好的老榆木，运回去能卖大价钱。他们拆一根，崖上就簌簌往下掉一层沙。

Half an old plank walkway clings to a low cliff, its beams socketed one by one into holes in the rock. Swordsmen hired by a timber merchant from inside the Pass are dismantling it and stacking the beams on carts: fine old elm, they say, worth a lot back home. Every beam they pull out brings a curtain of sand pattering down the cliff.
after: 刀手们被赶跑，你们看了看车上的梁，每根梁头都烙着同一个印：「千里 丁未冬」。原来这截栈道是千里号的人修的，修了十年，梁还没朽。你们把梁一根根插了回去，崖不掉沙了。

With the swordsmen chased off you look at the beams on the cart. Every beam end bears the same brand: 'Qianli, winter of Dingwei.' The Qianli caravan built this walkway, and after ten years the beams haven't rotted. You fit them back into their sockets one by one, and the cliff stops shedding sand.

name: 掏崖户
Cliff Burrowers
before: 一面土红色的崖壁被掏出了十几个洞，一伙逃兵住在里面，嫌洞小就往里再掏，嫌冷就在洞里生火，熏得崖面一片黑。崖脚已经掉下来好几块，他们照掏不误。附近的人说，每天夜里，总有人来把他们白天掏的洞拿泥巴填上一点，第二天他们又掏开。

A reddish cliff has been dug into a dozen holes, and a band of deserters lives in them. When a hole is too small they dig deeper, when it's cold they light fires inside, and the cliff face is blackened with smoke. Chunks have already fallen from its foot and they keep digging. Locals say that every night someone comes and fills a little of what they dug that day with mud, and the next day they dig it out again.
after: 逃兵被赶走了。洞壁上填过的地方一层泥一层草，抹得很匀，泥里掺着骆驼毛。最里面的一处泥上，有人用指甲刻了一只小骆驼，四条腿，一条腿是弯的。夜里来补崖的，是个懂行的人。

The deserters are driven out. Where the holes were filled, the work is mud and straw in even layers, with camel hair mixed in. On the innermost patch someone has scratched a little camel with a fingernail, four legs, one of them bent. Whoever comes at night to mend the cliff knows the trade.

name: 冬棚林
Winter Camp Wood
before: 胡杨林深处有一片平地，地上挖着一排排浅坑，坑边垒着矮墙，像是有很多人在这里过过冬。如今一群野猪占了这里，拱得满地是坑，见人就冲。一棵老胡杨的树杈上，横担着一根刻满了道道的木梁。

Deep in the poplar wood is a flat clearing dug with rows of shallow pits, each with a low wall around it, as if a great many people once wintered here. Now a sounder of wild boar has taken it over, rooting the ground into craters and charging anyone who comes near. Across a fork in an old poplar lies a beam covered in tally marks.
after: 野猪被赶进了林子深处。你们取下那根木梁，上面是一冬天的工账，刻得一笔一画：「运石三千担，抹泥九百丈，修栈道七十丈，补窟顶十一处。」落款「千里号驼队」。坑一共三百个，那年冬天，三百人就睡在这里，白天上崖干活。

The boar are driven deep into the woods. You take down the beam. It holds a whole winter's work account, carved stroke by stroke: 'Stone carried, three thousand loads. Plaster laid, nine hundred zhang. Walkway built, seventy zhang. Cave ceilings repaired, eleven.' Signed 'Qianli caravan, camel train'. There are three hundred pits. That winter the three hundred slept here and worked on the cliff by day.

name: 驱鬼班
The Exorcists
before: 崖下的村子闹「凿鬼」：每到半夜，崖里就传出叮叮的凿石声，第二天崖上就多一块新补的泥。一伙跳大神的驱鬼班子跑来，收了全村的钱，在崖下堆了一大垛柴火，说要放火把崖里的鬼熏出来。村民拦也不是，不拦也不是。

The village below the cliff is haunted by a 'chisel ghost': every midnight the clink of a chisel sounds inside the cliff, and the next day there's a fresh patch of plaster on the rock. A troupe of shamanic exorcists has turned up, taken the whole village's money and stacked a great pile of firewood at the cliff foot, meaning to smoke the ghost out. The villagers don't know whether to stop them.
after: 驱鬼班子被打散，柴火堆拆了。你们攀上去看那些「鬼补」的地方：裂缝里楔着木楔，外头抹着泥，泥上压着指印，是一只粗大的人手，指印旁边照例刻着一只小骆驼。村里一个老汉嘟囔：「哪有鬼这么勤快，补了十年。」

The exorcists scattered and the woodpile taken apart, you climb up to look at the ghost's repairs: wooden wedges driven into the cracks, mud smoothed over them, fingerprints pressed in by a big rough human hand, and beside them, as always, a little scratched camel. An old villager grumbles, 'What ghost works that hard? Ten years of patching.'

name: 崖规牌
The Cliff Rules
before: 崖脚立着一块木牌，上面写着五条规矩：「一、崖下不许泼水。二、窟里不许生火。三、刮西风的日子不许上栈道。四、夜里听见崖里有凿石声，不要应，也不要去看。五、看见崖上有骆驼，给它让路。」一队金面弩手守着木牌，谁犯一条就放一箭。今天几个醉醺醺的商贩偏要试试，拎着水桶往崖上泼。

A board at the cliff foot lists five rules: '1. No splashing water at the foot of the cliff. 2. No fires in the caves. 3. No going on the walkways on days when the west wind blows. 4. If you hear chiselling inside the cliff at night, don't answer and don't go to look. 5. If you see a camel on the cliff, give way to it.' A troop of Gold Mask crossbowmen guards the board and looses an arrow at anyone who breaks a rule. Today some drunken traders are bent on testing it and are sloshing buckets of water up the rock.
after: 商贩和弩手都散了，老石匠给你们讲：这崖是砾岩，卵石和沙子靠泥和石灰胶在一起，凿窟像切冻糕；可水一渗，胶就化，墙说酥就酥。烟熏黑壁画。西风卷沙，一刮就磨掉一层崖面。至于凿石声和骆驼，老石匠笑了：「那是崖上的一个人。」

Traders and crossbowmen gone, an old stonemason explains. The cliff is conglomerate, pebbles and sand held together by clay and lime, so carving it is like slicing jelly; but once water seeps in, the glue softens and a wall can crumble. Smoke blackens the murals. The west wind drives sand that scours a layer off the face every time it blows. As for the chiselling and the camel, the old man smiles. 'That's a man who lives up on the cliff.'

name: 苇篱梁
Reed Fence Ridge
before: 林边的沙梁上插着一道道芦苇篱笆，一排接一排，像梳子的齿，把西边刮来的沙挡在崖顶外面。一伙驼贩子的伙计正在拔篱笆，把芦苇捆成捆喂骆驼，拔了一大片，沙子已经顺着缺口往崖顶上流了。

On the sand ridge at the edge of the wood stand rows of reed fences, rank after rank like the teeth of a comb, keeping the sand blown from the west off the top of the cliff. A camel dealer's hands are pulling them up and bundling the reeds for camel fodder. They've cleared a large patch, and sand is already trickling through the gap toward the clifftop.
after: 驼贩子的伙计被打跑，你们把芦苇一捆捆插了回去。篱笆桩子底下埋着一块小木牌：「丁未冬，千里号扎苇篱十二道。沙不上崖，窟顶不压。」桩子是旧的，芦苇却是新的，有人年年来换。

The camel hands chased off, you plant the reeds back bundle by bundle. Buried at the foot of a post is a small wooden tag: 'Winter of Dingwei. Twelve reed fences set by the Qianli caravan. Keep the sand off the cliff and it won't crush the cave roofs.' The posts are old but the reeds are new. Someone replaces them every year.

name: 绞盘营
Winch Camp
before: 山脚扎着一座大营，营中间立着一架巨大的木绞盘，粗绳一直通到崖顶，从前是往崖上吊木料和石料的。一伙雇佣兵占了这里，步、弩、骑都有，拿绞盘把抢来的货往崖上的空窟里吊，当成了他们的仓库。绞盘吱吱嘎嘎地转，绳子磨得快断了。

A big camp at the foot of the hills, and at its centre a huge wooden windlass whose thick rope runs all the way to the clifftop; it once hoisted timber and stone. Mercenaries, foot, crossbow and horse, have taken it over and use it to haul their loot up into an empty cave they treat as a warehouse. The windlass squeals and groans, and the rope is nearly worn through.
after: 雇佣兵被打散，你们换下了快断的绳子。绞盘的轴上刻着一行字：「老凿造，千里号三百人共推。」旁边还有一行小的，像是后来补的：「一人推不动，三百人推得动。」附近的石匠说，老凿是修了一辈子窟的老匠头，如今住在山脚的死胡同里，「脾气比石头还硬」。

The mercenaries scattered, you replace the fraying rope. Carved on the windlass axle: 'Made by Lao Zao. Turned by the three hundred of the Qianli caravan.' Beside it, smaller, as if added later: 'One man can't turn it. Three hundred can.' Lao Zao, the local masons say, means Old Chisel, a master carver who has repaired caves all his life and now lives down a dead end at the foot of the hills. 'Harder-headed than stone.'

name: 青金帐
The Lapis Tent
before: 一顶靛蓝色的帐篷，帐主是个粟特女商，卖的是青金石：从西边几千里外的山里运来，磨成粉就是壁画上最贵的蓝。一伙兵痞围着她的帐篷，非说她的石头是染的，要「没收验货」。女商人坐在帐里纹丝不动，手里转着一块蓝石头：「谁认得出真假，我就卖给谁。」

An indigo tent belongs to a Sogdian woman who sells lapis lazuli, brought from mountains thousands of miles west and ground into the costliest blue on any mural. A gang of soldier-thugs surrounds her tent insisting her stones are dyed and must be 'confiscated for inspection'. She sits inside without moving, turning a blue stone in her fingers. 'I'll sell to whoever can tell real from fake.'
after: 兵痞被打跑，女商人倒也爽快：「真货里有金星，像夜里的天。」她开了张，跟你们换货。她说十年前千里号在她这里买过一大袋青金，要给一座窟画顶，「三百个人头顶上，要一片真的蓝天」。姓吴的老画匠来过好几回，买不起，摸一摸就走，「下回来，我赊给他」。

With the thugs chased off she's cheerful enough. 'The real stone has gold flecks in it, like the night sky.' She opens for trade. Ten years ago, she says, the Qianli caravan bought a big bag of lapis from her to paint a cave ceiling: 'a real blue sky over three hundred heads'. And an old painter called Wu has come by several times, couldn't afford it, only touched the stones and left. 'Next time he comes, I'll give it him on credit.'

name: 渗水窟
The Seeping Cave
before: 山脚一个小窟里，壁画正一片片往下剥：窟顶在渗水，水顺着墙往下流，画上的飞天眼看就要没了脸。几个揭壁贼趁机拿湿毡子往墙上糊，说「反正要掉，不如我们揭了卖」。他们雇了几个打手守在窟口，谁来都说是在「抢救」。

In a small cave at the foot of the hill the murals are peeling away flake by flake: the ceiling is seeping, water runs down the walls, and the painted apsaras are about to lose their faces. A few mural peelers are taking advantage, pasting wet felt onto the wall: 'It's falling off anyway, might as well peel it and sell it.' Their hired toughs stand at the entrance telling everyone it's a 'rescue'.
after: 揭壁贼被赶走，你们爬上窟顶找漏水的来处：崖顶上有一道挖出来的排水沟，沟口被沙和枯草堵死了，雨水积在顶上，一点点往下渗。沟边的石头上刻着「千里号挖」。你们清开了沟，窟里不滴水了。千里号那年冬天修的，不光是栈道。

The peelers driven off, you climb above the cave to find where the water comes from. On the clifftop is a dug drainage channel, its mouth choked with sand and dead grass, so rain pools on top and seeps down bit by bit. A stone by the channel is carved 'Dug by the Qianli caravan'. You clear it, and the cave stops dripping. That winter the caravan mended more than walkways.

name: 栈脚营
The Walkway Foot
before: 一道长长的栈道从崖脚一直攀到崖腰，栈道脚下扎着一营金面骑卫，马拴了一排，人守在台阶口。他们不许任何人上栈道，也不许任何人拆栈道，前些天有个木材商想来量量木头，被他们连人带尺子扔进了河里。

A long plank walkway climbs from the foot of the cliff to its waist, and at its base camps a company of Gold Mask riders, horses tethered in a row, men posted at the bottom step. They let no one up the walkway and let no one take it apart. A few days ago a timber merchant came to measure the wood and they threw him, ruler and all, into the river.
after: 骑卫们被打退，领头的捂着胳膊说：「这条栈道是那三百个驼夫修的。洞主说，栈道在，他们回来就有路走。」他朝崖腰努努嘴：「上面住着一个人，洞主不让我们碰他，也不让别人碰他。他要什么，我们就往上送什么。」

The riders beaten back, their leader holds his arm and says: 'Those three hundred camel men built this walkway. The Lord says while it stands, they'll have a road when they come back.' He jerks his chin at the cliff's waist. 'A man lives up there. The Lord won't let us touch him, or let anyone else. Whatever he asks for, we send up.'

name: 拓碑崖
Rubbing Cliff
before: 山脚的崖壁上刻着一方题记，几个拓碑贼正拿墨包往纸上拍，拓一张卖一张，生怕拓坏了，还雇了一伙刀手在边上望风。为了拓得清楚，他们把题记上的石缝全用刀剔了一遍，越剔越深，石皮一块块往下掉。

An inscription is carved on the rock at the foot of the hill, and a few rubbing thieves are dabbing ink pads onto paper over it, a sheet to sell for every sheet they take, with hired swordsmen keeping watch. To get sharper rubbings they've been picking out the grooves with knives, deeper each time, and flakes of rock skin keep falling.
after: 拓碑贼被赶走，题记总算保住了。你们读下来：「丁未冬，千里号驼队三百人修崖于此，匠头老凿。驼户曹三，坠栈折腿，不能行，留山。」字是账房的字，一笔不苟。最后一行刻得浅一些：「留下的也是千里号的人。」

The rubbing thieves chased off, the inscription is saved. It reads: 'Winter of Dingwei. Three hundred of the Qianli camel train repaired the cliff here. Master mason: Lao Zao. Cao San, camel driver, fell from the walkway and broke his leg. Unable to travel, he stays on the mountain.' It's the bookkeeper's hand, every stroke precise. The last line is cut shallower: 'Those who stay behind are Qianli too.'
